claims.text: Spin-polarized density functional theory can be used to assess whether a material has a ferromagnetic ground state.
Ferromagnetic stability can be assessed by comparing the total energies of different spin configurations.
Spin-polarized DFT calculations can evaluate ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and non-magnetic spin arrangements.
Reliable magnetic-state calculations require experimentally determined or relaxed lattice parameters and an appropriate exchange-correlation functional.
Different spin alignments are associated with distinguishable electronic structures and densities of states.
A lower total energy for the ferromagnetic alignment than for competing spin arrangements indicates that ferromagnetic interactions are energetically favored.
A material has a ferromagnetic ground state when the parallel-spin configuration has the lowest calculated energy among the configurations considered.
Energies of non-ferromagnetic reference states provide a baseline for determining relative magnetic stability.
Accurate determination of the magnetic ground state requires sufficiently converged simulations.
Calculated magnetic-state results may differ near phase boundaries or under external fields.
The prediction is limited by exchange-correlation-functional approximations and by metastable states that may be omitted from the calculations.
Magnetometry such as SQUID measurements can experimentally characterize magnetic ordering.
